references.text: God forbids Noah and his descendants from eating meat with the blood in it, which is the seat of life. This is the first biblical commandment concerning blood.
A perpetual statute that forbids the Israelites from eating fat and blood, and emphasizes the holy character of the covenant of blood.
Repeats the prohibition against eating blood and warns that whoever does so shall be cut off from their people.
The context for the verse, which explains that blood is given to make atonement on the altar, and that the soul (נֶפֶשׁ) is in the blood.
Moses repeats the prohibition against eating blood and commands that it be poured out on the ground like water.
Emphasizes that the blood is the life (נֶפֶשׁ), and that one must not eat the life together with the meat.
Forbids eating the blood of firstborn animals; the blood shall be poured out on the ground.
Saul urges the people not to sin against the Lord by eating meat with the blood in it.
The Lord rebukes those who eat meat with the blood in it and says they will not inherit the land.
The Apostolic Council in Jerusalem requires Gentile Christians to abstain from blood, in accordance with the commandments of the Torah.
The apostles' letter to Gentile Christians forbids blood and what has been strangled.
Paul reminds them of the Apostolic Council's decision that Gentile Christians must keep away from blood.
